channel.title: Israel National News Flashes
channel.description: Latest news flashes from Israel National News

item.title: PM praises soldiers for successful Samaria weapons raid
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu commented, "I commend our forces on a successful operation in Samaria in which they destroyed dozens of lathes for weapons manufacturing, seized dozens of weapons, and arrested individuals wanted for involvement in terrorism." "​Our activity to thwart terrorism continues with full force in Judea and Samaria, Gaza, Lebanon, and every place where our enemies attempt to threaten the State of Israel."

item.title: Israeli indicted for working with foreign intelligence agents
item.description: Shin Bet investigation finds Israeli citizen operated for foreign intelligence elements, participated in activity against Israel.

item.description: IDF foils imminent terror attack, arrests five-man cell

item.title: IDF eliminates Nukhba commander who led October 7 Sufa attack
item.description: Hamas commander who led October 7 infiltration into Sufa outpost, participated in holding Israeli hostages, is eliminated in Khan Yunis.

item.description: Belgian union threatens strike over flights to Israel

item.title: Erin Piacenti, a new mother, named as victim of Manhattan stabbing
item.description: Erin Piacenti, 32-year-old VP of Bank of America vice president, named as woman killed while heading home after returning from maternity leave earlier this week.

item.title: IDF smashes 30 weapons workshops in Shechem
item.description: IDF destroys 30 weapon production machines in Shechem area, searching hundreds of sites and arresting dozens of suspects.

item.title: JD Vance refuses to disavow Tucker Carlson
item.description: US Vice President JD Vance refuses to distance himself from Tucker Carlson, saying he won’t 'throw friends under the bus.'

item.description: 11 Givati soldiers freed after APC storm

item.title: Poll boost for Netanyahu: Coalition climbs to 51 seats
item.description: Netanyahu bloc reaches its strongest showing since May as the Zionist opposition falls to 57 seats; Ofer Winter crosses the threshold with four.

item.title: Amb. Huckabee: Violence against Palestinians causes damage to Israel
item.description: US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee addressed Israeli violence against Palestinians in Judea and Samaria in an interview on Reshet Bet, saying that it reduced Israel's standing in the International community precisely when Israel is most in need of allies.

item.title: Standing firm, 25 years after September 11
item.description: Survival is not enough. There is also an obligation to preserve the truth about what happened.

item.title: Reserve general scraps plans for right-wing party
item.description: Lt. Col. (res.) Amir Aviv abandons plans to launch a new right-wing party, warning that too many competing lists could put the entire bloc’s path to victory at risk.

item.title: The Torah is a song - Are we listening?
item.description: Have we really been listening to the song? Have we allowed the Torah to speak to us again?

item.title: Foundation of repentance
item.description: It is supremely relevant that our national return to our homeland causes such paroxysms of fury among the nations of the world - and tragically among certain of our own people - who hate being confronted with the truth of the Torah’s decrees.

item.title: The immutable Esther Doctrine
item.description: Who could have imagined a politician cynically invoking the model of Esther to advocate for putting the Jewish people in danger in support of electing to power modern Haman-like enemies? Go out and vote to defeat those malign Jew-hating candidates. Opinion.

item.title: Iran has opened a new front - America’s Persian Gulf bases are now in the crosshairs
item.description: By targeting U.S. military positions across the Persian Gulf, Tehran is transforming a contained confrontation into a regional test of deterrence, escalation, and American resolve. Opinion.

item.title: Podcast: Better living conditions for Palestinians will not bring peace
item.description: A century of rejectionism shows economic improvements cannot substitute for accepting Israel’s existence, and warns of a growing anti-Israel trend in US politics.

item.title: South Korea reportedly preparing military deployment to Strait of Hormuz
item.description: South Korea is reportedly preparing to deploy military assets to the Strait of Hormuz, while Seoul says no final deployment decision has been made.

item.title: The new libel to destroy Israel
item.description: Anti-Israel libel of the month: Violence in the “West Bank" is being malevolently misrepresented. Opinion.

item.title: Syria begins destroying remnants of Assad-era chemical weapons program
item.description: Syria announces it has begun destroying remnants of Assad's chemical weapons program, with the UN verifying the destruction of 42 aerial bombs.

item.title: Trump: Iran was weeks away from nuclear weapon before US strikes
item.description: In an interview with British journalist Bev Turner, Trump says Iran was weeks from a nuclear weapon before US strikes, which destroyed key sites and left the regime in serious trouble.

item.title: Wave of departures from Yesh Atid continues: Karine Elharrar will not seek reelection
item.description: Another prominent departure: Former minister Karine Elharrar announces that she will not seek a Knesset seat with Yesh Atid in the next election.

item.title: Trump portrait appears on new US $1 coin marking America's 250th anniversary
item.description: President Trump's portrait appears on a new US $1 commemorative coin for America's 250th anniversary, despite a federal ban on living presidents.

item.title: 14 years after evacuation: Families return to Migron, outpost connected to power grid
item.description: Move kept under the radar for about a year: Several families have been living at a new agricultural outpost in Upper Migron, which was connected to the power grid on Thursday.

item.title: Attempted stabbing attack at Damascus Gate in Jerusalem, terrorist neutralized
item.description:
A terrorist attempted to stab a police officer at Damascus Gate in Jerusalem's Old City.
Police officers opened fire at the suspect and neutralized him. No injuries among police officers have been reported.

item.title: 78-year-old moderately injured in apartment building fire in Rishon LeZion
item.description:
A 78-year-old man was moderately injured and another person sustained minor injuries in a fire at a residential building in Rishon LeZion.
Magen David Adom (MDA) paramedics provided medical treatment and evacuated both victims to Shamir-Assaf Harofeh Hospital with signs of smoke inhalation.

item.title: US House passes bill cutting aid to colleges that participate in BDS boycotts
item.description: US House of Representatives passes bill that could cut federal student aid to colleges engaging in commercial or academic boycotts of Israel.
